'''Jeremy Nichol McNeil''' {{post-nominals|country=CAN|CM|FRSC}} (20 November 1944 – 18 July 2024) was a British-Canadian biologist and zoologist. In 2004, he was named the Helen Battle Professor of Chemical Ecology in the Biology Department at the [[University of Western Ontario]], having previously worked at [[Laval University]].

==Background==
McNeil was born in [[Tonbridge]], England on 20 November 1944. His family moved to [[Newfoundland]] in 1945, however, he returned to England for high school and worked for two years as a hospital orderly then as a wine merchant in London. He received his [[bachelor's degree]] from the [[University of Western Ontario]] in 1969 and his PhD at [[North Carolina State University]] in 1972.<ref name="entsoc">{{cite web |title=Jeremy N. McNeil, ESA Fellow (2015) |url=https://www.entsoc.org/fellows/mcneil |website=entsoc.org |publisher=[[Entomological Society of America]] |access-date=April 30, 2021}}</ref> McNeil died on 18 July 2024, at the age of 79.<ref>[https://affordablefuneraloptions.ca/tribute/details/1226/Jeremy-McNeil/obituary.html Obituary of Jeremy Nichol McNeil obituary]</ref>

==Career==
Upon completing his formal education, McNeil accepted a faculty position at [[Laval University]] from 1972 until 2002.<ref name="rsc">{{cite web |title=JEREMY MCNEIL, FRSC |url=https://rsc-src.ca/en/governance-programmes/council/jeremy-mcneil |website=rsc-src.ca |access-date=May 1, 2021}}</ref> In 1998, he received the [[The McNeil Medal|McNeil Medal]] from the [[Royal Society of Canada]] (RSC) as an "individual who has demonstrated an outstanding ability to promote and communicate science to students and the public within Canada."<ref>{{cite web |title=La Société royale du Canada souligne le travail de communicateur scientifique de l'entomologiste Jeremy McNeil en lui décernant la Médaille... McNeil |url=https://archives.nouvelles.ulaval.ca/Au.fil.des.evenements/1998/11.05/profil.html |website=archives.nouvelles.ulaval.ca |access-date=May 1, 2021 |language=French |date=May 5, 1998|url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210502163544/https://archives.nouvelles.ulaval.ca/Au.fil.des.evenements/1998/11.05/profil.html |archive-date=2021-05-02 }}</ref> He also became a Fellow of the [[Entomological Society of Canada]] and the [[Royal Society of Canada]] (RSC). McNeil left Laval in 2002 and was awarded a one-year Humboldt Research Fellowship with Drs. [[Wittko Francke]] and [[Stefan Schulz]]. In 2004, he was named the Helen Battle Professor of Chemical Ecology in the Biology Department at the [[University of Western Ontario]] (UWO).<ref name="entsoc"/> McNeil was appointed the scientific director of Western's Biotron in 2008 and served a three-year term before stepping down from the position in August 2011.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Winders |first1=Jason |title=Troubling yesterdays for building of tomorrow |url=https://news.westernu.ca/2012/01/troubling-yesterdays-for-building-of-tomorrow/ |website=news.westernu.ca |access-date=May 1, 2021 |date=January 19, 2012}}</ref> During this time, he was also the recipient of the [[Fry Medal]], given to a Canadian Zoologist who "has made an outstanding contribution to knowledge and understanding of an area in zoology."<ref>{{cite web |title=F. E. J. Fry Medal |url=https://csz-scz.ca/wp/award/fej-fry-award/ |website=csz-scz.ca |access-date=May 2, 2021 |date=February 29, 2020 |archive-date=December 13, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211213090018/https://csz-scz.ca/wp/award/fej-fry-award/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Upon stepping down as scientific director, McNeil was appointed to a Distinguished University Professorship which "acknowledges sustained excellence in scholarship over a substantial career at Western."<ref>{{cite web |last1=Mayne |first1=Paul |title=Western faculty earn top university distinctions |url=https://news.westernu.ca/2014/03/western-faculty-earn-top-university-distinctions/ |website=news.westernu.ca |access-date=May 2, 2021 |date=March 27, 2014}}</ref> In the same year, he was also named the recipient of the Science Ambassador Award as part of the 2014 Partners In Research National Awards.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Winders |first1=Jason |title=McNeil honoured for science research, outreach |url=https://news.westernu.ca/2014/04/mcneil-honoured-for-science-research-outreach-2/ |website=news.westernu.ca |access-date=May 2, 2021 |date=April 17, 2014}}</ref> McNeil was nationally recognized for his "contributions to the study of reproductive biology in insects and for his dedication to increasing public appreciation of science" with the [[Order of Canada]] in 2015.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Talbot |first1=Adela |title=Professor, alumni named to the Order of Canada |url=https://news.westernu.ca/2015/01/biology-professor-six-alumni-named-to-the-order-of-canada/ |website=news.westernu.ca |access-date=May 2, 2021 |date=January 5, 2015}}</ref> He was also elected as Fellow of the [[Entomological Society of America]] in 2015.<ref name="entsoc"/> In 2016, he received a $10,000 award through the [[Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council]]’s Individual Award for Science Promotion.<ref>{{cite web |title=Canada's science champions receive top honours from the Government of Canada |url=https://www.nserc-crsng.gc.ca/Media-Media/NewsDetail-DetailNouvelles_eng.asp?ID=912 |website=nserc-crsng.gc.ca |access-date=May 2, 2021 |date=May 15, 2017|url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200925043357/https://www.nserc-crsng.gc.ca/Media-Media/NewsDetail-DetailNouvelles_eng.asp?ID=912 |archive-date=2020-09-25 }}</ref>

During the [[COVID-19 pandemic]], McNeil was the co-recipient of the 2020 Hellmuth Prize for Achievement in Research which "recognizes faculty members with outstanding international reputations for their contributions in research."<ref>{{cite web |last1=Mayne |first1=Paul |title=Cheryl Forchuk, Jeremy McNeil earn 2020 Hellmuth Prizes |url=https://news.westernu.ca/2020/07/cheryl-forchuk-jeremy-mcneil-earn-2020-hellmuth-prizes/ |website=news.westernu.ca |access-date=May 1, 2021 |date=July 2, 2020}}</ref> He also received funding for her project ''"Monarch fall migration, overwintering mortality and the effects of defence compounds released by decomposing butterflies on the soil ecosystem.''"<ref>{{cite web |last1=Mayne |first1=Paul |title=Discovery Grants back 75 research projects |url=https://news.westernu.ca/2020/05/discovery-grants-back-75-western-research-projects/ |website=news.westernu.ca |access-date=May 1, 2021 |date=May 7, 2020}}</ref>
